target_customer: Consumers and small businesses needing a van or pickup for moves and hauling; hosts renting out trucks
problem: Renting trucks was slow and costly. The YC W15 company was a webinar tool (Breakout Room) that pivoted to self-service truck rental in 2016 and 2017.
business_model: Marketplace commission (20 percent from commercial hosts, 30 percent from peer hosts per TechCrunch 2022)

founders.name: Adam Steinberg
prior_employers: PlacePunch (own startup, sold to Silverpop and later IBM)

founders.name: Chris Glace
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him with no bio; a search summary says the idea came from his frustration renting trucks.

exit.reason: Not confirmed. One third party review site says a financial crisis hit in late 2023; no company announcement found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Phone unlock hardware, insurance and fleet operations for a small team; the original webinar tool was simpler.

defensibility.rationale: Marketplace supply and insurance arrangements could be copied; large rental firms partnered instead (Budget in 2019).

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Budget partnered with Fetch in 2019 per Auto Rental News; no evidence of a copy.

market_need_then: Founders cited their own pain renting trucks for moves in Atlanta. A 2017 pilot with a couple of trucks started in October 2016 and showed demand, per TechCrunch. No 2015 evidence for the original webinar idea.

branding.domain_note: Primary domain fetchtruck.com; an unrelated fetchpackage.com exists, a delivery startup with a similar name.

brand_strength.rationale: Short, friendly name that fit an on demand truck service, but generic and shared with other Fetch brands, and no press about the brand itself was found.

pivots.to: On demand truck and van rental
pivots.why: Webinar tool did not gain traction, per TechCrunch 2017; exact date approximate (about a year in, pilot in October)

pivots.to: Marketplace where outside owners rent trucks
pivots.why: Search summary of coverage; scale fleet without owning trucks

outcome_analysis: Fetch began in YC S15 as a webinar tool, pivoted into self-service truck rental, opened to third party fleets in 2018, and raised $3.5M in March 2022 led by NextView. It appears to have shut down around late 2023, but the only source is a review site and no cause is public, so no failure factor is assigned. The 24 person team size on YC and the 2022 expansion to several cities show real operations before the end.
notes: Round label conflict: Built In calls the $3.5M seed, Hypepotamus calls it Series A, TechCrunch gives no label, so stage is other. TechCrunch does not state a total raised. A search summary says Avis Budget Group is an investor, from an interview not opened. No pre 2022 round found; YC standard deal not recorded. Shutdown date and reason rest on one review site (sidehusl) and are unverified. Competitors empty: no dated rivals found for the 2015 webinar product, and the 2017 TechCrunch article names none. fetchtruck.com returned HTTP 503 and fetch search results show an app still listed, so shutdown is unconfirmed.
